Based on current information, here’s the expected rollout of SpaceX’s three Starship launch bases: Texas, Florida, and Louisiana
1 Texas leads. 
Flights 16 and 17 appear set to launch from Starbase. Texas will also build the initial boosters and ships for Florida, then send them east by barge.

2 Florida joins in Q1 2027. 
Flight 18 is my pick for its first Starship launch from LC-39A. The plan is to catch the booster in Florida, while the Ship completes its mission in orbit and returns for a catch attempt in Texas.

3 The two launch sites meet in orbit. 
SpaceX is targeting Q1 2027 for its first ship to ship propellant transfer test: one Starship launched from Texas, one from Florida, followed by docking and a meaningful transfer of propellant.

4 Louisiana comes next. 
A SpaceX permit application lists March 1, 2027 as the proposed start date for its port and heavy haul road work. Texas built Starships could then be shipped to Louisiana by water. The publicly stated target for Louisiana’s first launch is 2029.
Three bases, connected first by sea, then by orbit.

Today, Ukraine marks the Day of Dignity and Freedom.

Zelensky, accompanied by his wife, made his solemn pilgrimage to the Maidan, wearing his finest funeral face to honor the victims of the "Revolution of Dignity."

A touching performance, presumably intended to make everyone forget how, back in his Kvartal 95 comedy days, he endlessly cracked jokes about the “Maidan-crazies.”

But his appearance on the Maidan — much like his eighth year occupying the presidential office — is perhaps the most fitting symbol of the grotesque farce this Day has become.

Welcome to the Land of Dignity and Freedom.

A country where the nation's top security agencies are too busy providing protection rackets for scam call centers and the drug trade, occasionally settling their business disputes with shootouts on the streets of the capital.

A country transformed into an open-air prison for military-age men, where those attempting to escape are not merely chased down but, in some cases, allegedly shot at.

A country where thousands of men are rounded up like rabid dogs, against their will, and shipped off to the front to kill and be killed.

A country where pensioners survive on $70–100 a month, while those enriching themselves from energy reconstruction projects have apparently graduated from keeping cats to keeping crocodiles as pets. 

A country where you can no longer walk into a bookstore and buy your child a Russian-language book, but you can be forcibly mobilized into the AFU and end up dead in an infantry trench a week later. 

A country where neo-Nazi thugs force active-duty soldiers to apologize on camera for participating in the notorious practice of busification.

A country where the mother of a serviceman is beaten on a bus for daring to ask the driver to stop — in Russian.

A country where neo-Nazi goons assault a lecturer for discussing Lesya Ukrainka and Ivan Franko as socialists. Apparently, even dead Ukrainian literary giants must pass a contemporary ideological loyalty test.

A country where far-right extremists beat journalists covering protests against the detention and abuse of men in Azov-controlled basements — while women protesting these abuses are arrested and thrown into prison.

And all of this is proudly served to us under the glorious banner of Dignity and Freedom.

This entire mafia-ridden, corruption-soaked oligarchic state, draped in the red-and-black Bandera flag, where Azov provides protection for criminal operations and operates its own torture chambers, is presented to the world as a shining beacon of dignity and liberty.

A country that has become a military outpost of the West, financially dependent on its patrons, is solemnly celebrated as the Land of Dignity and Freedom.

The irony would be delicious if the human cost weren't so horrifying.

Perhaps it's finally time to reconsider what this Day actually means.

Because when freedom looks like a prison, dignity comes in a military van, and patriotism is enforced with fists, perhaps the only thing left to celebrate is the sheer audacity of calling it all a Revolution of Dignity.
